items.stem: A job takes 2 minutes for 1,000 items. It compares every item with every other item. How long does it take for 2,000 items?

options.text: About 4 minutes, because twice the items takes twice the time.
options.feedback: That rule fits a job that looks at each item once. This job compares pairs.

options.text: About 2 minutes, because the method is the same.
options.feedback: The method is the same, and the number of steps still grows with the list.

options.text: About 8 minutes, because doubling the list quadruples the steps.
options.feedback: Comparing every pair takes n times n steps. Twice the items makes four times the comparisons, and 4 times 2 minutes is 8 minutes.

items.stem: A page asks one question for the course list and one more for each course, at 5 milliseconds a question. With 40 courses it loads in about 0.2 seconds. What should the developer expect with 4,000 courses?

options.text: About 20 seconds, because the questions grow in step with the courses.
options.feedback: 4,001 questions at 5 milliseconds each take about 20,000 milliseconds. That is 100 times the courses and about 100 times the time.

options.text: About 0.2 seconds, because the page code does not change.
options.feedback: The code is the same, and the number of questions follows the number of courses.

options.text: The page stops working, because the list is too long.
options.feedback: The page keeps working. It gets slower in step with the courses.

items.stem: A startup's report takes 1 second for 1,000 customers. It compares every customer with every other customer. The company expects 100,000 customers next year. What is the sensible reaction?

options.text: Relax. A hundred times more customers means about 100 seconds.
options.feedback: That estimate fits a job that looks at each customer once. This job compares pairs.

options.text: Plan a different method. The time grows about ten thousand times, to nearly 3 hours.
options.feedback: A hundred times more customers makes about 100 times 100, or 10,000 times, more comparisons. 10,000 seconds is about 2.8 hours.

options.text: Buy a server twice as fast and keep the method.
options.feedback: A server twice as fast cuts a 10,000-fold increase to 5,000-fold. The report still takes over an hour.

items.stem: Finding a number in a sorted list of 1,000,000 numbers by halving takes about 20 steps. The list grows to 2,000,000 numbers. About how many steps does it take?

options.feedback: That rule fits a job that looks at each number once. Halving does not double its steps.
A search by halving does not compare pairs, so this estimate is far too high.

options.text: About 2,000,000, because the search must look at every number.
options.feedback: Halving throws away half of the remaining numbers at each step, so it never looks at them all.

options.text: About 21, because each doubling adds one step.
options.feedback: One extra halving covers a list twice as long, so the steps go from 20 to 21.
